traditions.name: Old Quad and the Eight-Hour Day
traditions.description: The Old Quad was the university's first building, and in 1856 the stonemasons building it downed tools and joined the marches that won the eight-hour working day. Visitors can walk through the Old Quad, the campus's historic heart.

traditions.name: Spot the Old Arts clock oddity
traditions.description: Students and visitors are invited to study the Roman numerals on the Old Arts Building clock tower and spot what is odd about them.

traditions.name: The last piece of the original fence
traditions.description: A single segment of the wrought-iron fence that once encircled the whole campus survives outside the Medical Building. The grounds were opened to the public in exchange for free gas lighting from the City of Melbourne; visitors can find the remaining fence section.

details.airportInfo: Melbourne Airport at Tullamarine is about 20 km north-west of the Parkville campus. The SkyBus runs to Southern Cross Station in the city, a short tram ride from the university.
details.funFact: One campus walk covers a century of Australian architecture: Victorian Gothic labs from the 1880s, Walter Burley Griffin's Newman College, Australia's first purpose-built university library and Roy Grounds' Brutalist John Medley Building.
details.languageInfo: The university's Latin motto, Postera crescam laude, means 'I shall grow in the esteem of future generations'.
details.transportationFact: Trams run up Swanston Street from the city centre to the university's front door. The Parkville campus itself is compact and easy to explore on foot.

buildings.name: Old Pathology Building
buildings.description: Built in 1885 by Reed, Henderson & Smart, this early English Gothic building has been in continuous university use for well over a century. Now named the Elisabeth Murdoch Building, it is on the Victorian Heritage Register.

buildings.name: Newman College
buildings.description: American architects Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin built this college between 1916 and 1918, with a domed dining room between two stone residential wings. They even designed its chairs and tables, and it is on the Australian National Heritage List as one of the best examples of Griffin's work.
buildings.architect: Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin

buildings.name: Chemistry Building
buildings.description: Percy Edgar Everett of the Victorian Public Works Department designed this Collegiate Gothic teaching building in 1938, during the university's big interwar expansion. It still houses the School of Chemistry.

buildings.name: Baillieu Library
buildings.description: Australia's first purpose-built university library, designed by architecture lecturer John Scarborough and opened in 1959. Its foundations were laid strong enough for a tower of up to 19 storeys that was never built.
buildings.architect: John Scarborough, Ian Watkins and Barry Axtens
buildings.address: Corner of Grattan Street and Royal Parade, Parkville VIC

buildings.name: John Medley Building
buildings.description: Sir Roy Grounds designed this Brutalist block, built from 1969 to 1971 to relieve the crowded Old Arts Building. Its two six-storey towers rise above a five-storey base.

traditions.name: The Quadrangle jacaranda
traditions.description: Campus folklore says any student who has not started studying before the Quadrangle's jacaranda flowers will fail their exams. Visitors can see the tree (a clone of the 1928 original) bloom purple in late spring, a favourite photo backdrop.

traditions.name: War Memorial Carillon recitals
traditions.description: The clock tower holds the War Memorial Carillon, dedicated in 1928 and one of only three carillons in Australia. Visitors can hear live recitals at lunchtime (outside exam periods and public holidays).

traditions.name: Spot the kangaroo gargoyle
traditions.description: Among the Quadrangle's many gargoyles are Australian animals, including a kangaroo on the clock tower and kookaburras above the northern foyer entrance. Visitors can look for them around the sandstone buildings.

traditions.name: Graffiti Tunnel
traditions.description: The Graffiti Tunnel began as a student protest against the Vietnam War and is now a constantly changing living artwork. Visitors can walk through and see the latest layers of student art.

details.airportInfo: Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport is about 10 km south of the Camperdown campus. Trains from the airport reach Redfern Station, a short walk from the university.
details.funFact: Edmund Blacket's sandstone Main Quadrangle was begun in 1854, and Anthony Trollope called its Great Hall 'the finest chamber in the colonies'. The quadrangle was only finished in 1966, with the West Tower.
details.languageInfo: The Latin motto, Sidere mens eadem mutato, is translated by the university as 'the stars change, the mind remains the same'. Alumnus Clive James joked that it implies Sydney is really Oxford or Cambridge displaced 12,000 miles.
details.transportationFact: Redfern Station is a short walk from the campus, and buses run along Parramatta Road and City Road from the city centre.

buildings.name: University of Sydney Quadrangle
buildings.description: A Sydney sandstone quadrangle in Victorian Academic Gothic Revival, begun by Edmund Blacket in the 1850s and completed with the West Tower in 1966. It is the heritage-listed heart of the Camperdown campus.
buildings.architect: Edmund Blacket, James Barnet, Walter Liberty Vernon and Leslie Wilkinson

buildings.wiki: Great Hall of the University of Sydney
buildings.name: Great Hall of the University of Sydney
buildings.description: Completed in 1859 by Edmund Blacket, this Gothic Revival hall of stained glass, gables and gargoyles hosts graduations and recitals. Anthony Trollope thought no Oxford or Cambridge college had a hall with proportions so good.

buildings.name: Chau Chak Wing Museum
buildings.description: Johnson Pilton Walker's five-storey museum, completed in 2020, has four levels of exhibition space, including the Macleay and Nicholson galleries. A replica of an Aboriginal petroglyph of two wallabies greets visitors in the forecourt.

buildings.name: Charles Perkins Centre
buildings.description: Francis-Jones Morehen Thorp's research hub, opened in 2014, is built around a full-height atrium with a sweeping spiral staircase. It is named for Charles Perkins, the first man of Aboriginal descent to graduate from an Australian university.
buildings.architect: Francis-Jones Morehen Thorp with Building Studio
buildings.address: Royal Prince Alfred Hospital precinct, Camperdown NSW
